quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: A motorcyclist should constantly look ahead for:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Look ahead to stay alert to changing traffic, hazardous road conditions, and escape routes. Be ready to react quickly.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes since it is light outside.
Wear bright clothes so other motorists can see you better.
Be comfortable, wearing shorts if it is hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so other motorists can see you better.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright clothing when riding so other drivers can see you clearly, even in daylight.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.correctAnswerText: Cause control problems.
questions.explanation: Locking your brakes causes control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again. If your rear brake locks on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns that the signal will soon turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if safe. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid line means do not pass. A dashed line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Having only one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: Will not lead to a DUI conviction.
Will never affect your riding skills.
Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. You can be convicted of impaired riding even if you are below the legal blood alcohol limit.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to be more visible when riding, even during the day. Reflective materials also help.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather boots
questions.explanation: Leather boots provide the best protection when riding. Choose boots that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane is ending.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket if it is cold outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket.
questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding, even if the weather is warm.

questions.question: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. U.S. motorcycles made after 1978 turn on automatically when running. Always check that your headlight works before you ride.

questions.question: As a rider, you can reduce your chances of an accident by:

options.text: Refraining from using turn signals, as doing so could distract other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Being visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid collisions, be visible to others, use turn signals clearly, keep safe distance from other vehicles, watch ahead for danger, and be ready to react. Always stay alert.

questions.question: After riding over an object on the road, you should:

options.text: Continue riding because the danger has passed.
Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop to remove the object from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: Pull off the road and check your tires and rims for damage. Also check that nothing is caught in the chain or belt before you continue.

questions.question: When riding an unfamiliar motorcycle for the first time, you should:

options.text: Just start riding. There is no better way to learn than by doing.
Just start riding. Most bikes are similar, so you don't have to take the time to identify safety features.
Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn the bike's gear pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn the bike's gear pattern.
questions.explanation: Every bike is different. Before riding, do a safety check. Find where everything is. Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how the bike works.

questions.question: When cars are merging from an entrance ramp:

options.text: A motorcyclist should assume the entering drivers see them.
A motorcyclist should never assume the entering drivers see them.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should never assume the entering drivers see them.
questions.explanation: Never assume entering drivers see you. Give them plenty of space. Change lanes away if you can. If not, slow down to let them merge safely.

questions.question: Wearing which color will make you less visible to other motorists?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or drab colors while riding.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake at the same time as the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front brake at the same time as the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Apply controlled pressure to both brakes at the same time for the best stop. Be careful not to lock the brakes.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, you should ensure that it:
questions.correctAnswerText: Has no cracks or defects.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It must fit snugly and be free of cracks, loose padding, and frayed straps.

questions.question: Mirrors on motorcycles:

options.text: Have blind spots, just like cars.
Do not have blind spots because a motorcycle is usually smaller than a car

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you approach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal that the other vehicle should proceed.
You should continue through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots.
questions.explanation: Leather boots protect your feet the most when riding. Choose boots that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
It can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see as far as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: How do you become sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: The only way to sober up is to wait. Your body needs time to remove the alcohol. Nothing else will speed this up.

questions.question: How is alcohol different from other substances?

options.text: It enters the bloodstream very quickly.
It must be digested before entering the bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: It enters the bloodstream very quickly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It goes directly through the stomach and small intestine into the bloodstream and quickly affects the brain.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, what should you focus on most?
questions.correctAnswerText: Protection.
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing to consider when choosing a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider do to reduce collision risk?

options.text: Keep enough space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Ride down the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance around your motorcycle at all times. Maintain this space when following vehicles, being followed, passing, being passed, or sharing a lane.

questions.question: What should you look for in a protective motorcycle jacket?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather or strong synthetic material.
questions.explanation: Wear a protective jacket when riding. Choose one made of leather or sturdy synthetic material that covers your arms, fits snugly, and allows you to move freely. Built-in body armor offers the best protection.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Focus only on what is in front of you.
Focus only on what is behind you.
Be aware of what is in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be aware of what is in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: Pay attention to what is ahead of you, but also check your mirrors often to know what is behind you.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
Stop only if other traffic requires it.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.
